title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 750–754 of the sequel to La Longue Marche). Pi is a profinite Teichmüller-type fundamental group: a geometric pi_1 of a surface or moduli space. The fraktur group (read here as S, transcription has G) is an intermediate group, and M is the 'Galois–Teichmüller' group: an extension of a quotient Gamma of Gal(Qbar/Q), or of an anticipated Galois–Teichmüller group, by the geometric part. These form a chain Pi ⊂ S ⊂ M with quotients T = S/Pi, Gamma = M/S, N = M/Pi.

On the previous page Grothendieck takes a homomorphism M → G(Q) (here G(A_Q), adelic points) into a linear algebraic group G over Q. He defines Pi_Q ⊂ S_Q ⊂ M_Q as the Zariski closures of the images. These are normal in M_Q and give quotient group schemes T_Q, Gamma_Q, N_Q and the exact sequence (38) 1 → T_Q → N_Q → Gamma_Q → 1. The cyclotomic character chi_c : G → G_m is surjective and factors through Gamma_Q (39).

This page has two parts.

(a) Definition. The system of Q-group schemes (36), (37) is considered together with the homomorphism of chains (40) Pi → Pi_Q(A_Q), S → S_Q(A_Q), M → M_Q(A_Q) induced by M → G(A_Q). When conditions 1°)–4°) of an earlier page hold (a 'Lie homomorphism'), the datum is called an 'approximation de Lie' of the anticipated Galois–Teichmüller system. In modern terms this is a Zariski-dense representation of the arithmetic fundamental group / Galois–Teichmüller tower into a pro-algebraic group over Q (adelically), compatible with the geometric/arithmetic filtration and with the cyclotomic character. This is essentially the setting later formalised as relative and weighted completion.

(b) Construction. Take a homomorphism (41) T_0 → Pi, where T_0 is a free abelian group of finite type ('nid T_0' in the margin). The likely reading is the group generated by commuting Dehn twists of a pants decomposition or a 'nest' of curves, i.e. the inertia of a maximal degeneration. Composing with the L-structure Pi → Pi_Q(Q) gives (42) T_0 → Pi_Q(Q).
- By (21) p. 747', this homomorphism is quasi-unipotent, analogous to the monodromy theorem for twists.
- Hence it defines a homomorphism of group schemes. The next page gives (43) K_i : G_{a,Q} ⊗_Z T_0 → Pi_Q, a homomorphism of schemes in groups, not merely of abstract groups.
- This is obtained from the unipotent parts via the logarithm on a finite-index subgroup.
- Over all conjugates and open subgroups this gives a finite family of such 'Lie tori'. These are additive vector groups attached to degeneration data, i.e. the images of the cusp/boundary inertia in the completion.

Purpose: to build, inside an algebraic (Lie) approximation of the Teichmüller tower, the additive subgroups corresponding to the boundary strata. This would allow a Lie-algebraic or algebraic-group description of the 'Lego' gluing structure of the tower, with the Galois action controlled by chi_c.
errors: A quasi-unipotent homomorphism T_0 → Pi_Q(Q) does not itself factor through a homomorphism G_a ⊗ T_0 → Pi_Q. Only its restriction to a finite-index subgroup on which the images are unipotent does, taking 1/n·log of the n-th power. The semisimple, finite-order parts are lost. The next page's indexing 'by open subgroups' suggests Grothendieck is aware of this, but on this page the passage is stated loosely.
Notational inconsistency in (40): Pi_Q(A'_Q) versus A_Q elsewhere. The homomorphism of 'schémas en groupes' sentence breaks off at the page end and is completed on the next page as (43).
Conditions 1°)–4°) defining a 'Lie homomorphism' are on an earlier page not available here, so the definition cannot be fully checked.

ideas.what: 'Approximation de Lie' of the Galois–Teichmüller system: a Zariski-dense homomorphism of the chain Pi ⊂ S ⊂ M into adelic points of a chain of Q-algebraic groups Pi_Q ⊂ S_Q ⊂ M_Q, with the cyclotomic character factoring through the arithmetic quotient Gamma_Q → G_m
ideas.modern_name: Relative / weighted completion of arithmetic fundamental groups and mapping class groups (Galois action via motivic or pro-algebraic envelope)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (1989, P^1 minus 3 points); Hain (relative completion, 1990s); Hain–Matsumoto (weighted completion, 2003; relative pro-l completion of mapping class groups, 2009)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions the Lie-algebra / 'algebraic' aspect of the Teichmüller tower only vaguely; this precise definition appears unpublished

ideas.what: Images of Dehn-twist (or 'nest') abelian subgroups T_0 → Pi in the algebraic envelope are quasi-unipotent, hence give homomorphisms of group schemes G_a ⊗ T_0 → Pi_Q (vector-group 'Lie tori' attached to degenerations)
ideas.modern_name: Unipotence of Dehn twists in relative completion; logarithms of boundary monodromy; Ihara/Nakamura tangential-base-point inertia
ideas.usually_credited_to: Hain (relative completion of mapping class groups); Nakamura, Ihara, Matsumoto on boundary inertia

ideas.what: Zariski closures of images giving normal subgroup schemes and an exact sequence 1 → T_Q → N_Q → Gamma_Q → 1
ideas.modern_name: Algebraic envelope / Zariski closure of a representation

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up an algebraic-group ('Lie') approximation of the full Galois–Teichmüller tower. It is adelic, compatible with the geometric/arithmetic filtration, and the cyclotomic character factors through the arithmetic algebraic quotient. This is essentially the framework of weighted/relative completion, developed independently a decade or more later.
missed.quote: s'appellera aussi une "approximation de Lie" du système de Galois-Teichmüller anticipé
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents that Grothendieck anticipated the Hain–Matsumoto style pro-algebraic approach to the Galois action on mapping class groups. It also shows he combined it with boundary data, which may guide reading of the remaining unpublished Longue Marche material.

missed.claim: He proposes attaching to each 'nest' or degeneration subgroup T_0 a homomorphism of group schemes G_a ⊗ T_0 → Pi_Q. These would serve as a finite set of generating 'Lie tori', presumably to describe Pi_Q (and its Galois action) by gluing data. This is a Lie-algebraic version of the Lego / two-level principle.
missed.quote: On voit ((21) p. 747') que cet homomorphisme est quasi-unipotent, et qu'il définit par suite un homom. de schémas en groupes
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A presentation of relative completions of mapping class groups generated by boundary-twist vector groups, with Galois equivariance, links to Hain's and Brown's work on motivic structures and to the open question of Lie-algebraic GT for higher genus.

deep.surprise_reason: A clear early definition of an algebraic/Lie approximation of the Galois–Teichmüller tower, with the twist-unipotence construction. The conceptual idea (pro-algebraic completion) is now standard and was developed independently by Deligne and Hain. It is notable as an unpublished anticipation but not a hidden theorem.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: the mark is a tick/check, with 'sur Q' inserted above; '(36, 137)' should read '(36), (37)'.
The middle group in the chain is a fraktur S (matching the previous page), not fraktur G; line 3 reads 'Π ⊂ 𝔖 ⊂ M'.
In (42) the target is underlined: T_0 → \underline{Π}(Q), i.e. \underline{Π}_Q(Q).

Margin note is largely illegible; it seems to justify the definition/denomination of \underline{Π}_Q and mentions 'nid T_0' (nest), 'W*' and a 'merveilleux droit'. 'Grothendieck' in the margin reading is doubtful.
